title: Map VA/DoD suicide-risk guidance to snapshot decisions
proposedRouting: Review one rule family at a time: observable suicide-related facts, information that must be obtained for a selected disposition, and disposition consequences. Keep screening, assessment, formulation, intervention, and disposition distinct in the trace.
guidance: The official 2024 VA/DoD guideline and its locally extracted, gitignored document are available. Decide which small set of structured observations belongs in PsychSim's question-bank snapshot and which findings can justify outpatient care, urgent evaluation, or emergency transfer. Do not import a longitudinal care protocol or reduce disposition to a single score. Missing information must remain unknown, and a single underlying mistake should receive only its worst applicable consequence.
reviewerNotes: Psychiatrist/developer direction: use a staged History workflow. General psychiatric history includes a concise routine suicide-safety screen. A separate purchasable Suicide and self-harm assessment reveals the complete structured question set, including passive versus active ideation, intent, plan, recent preparatory behavior or attempt, access to means, prior attempts, and applicable acute modifiers. The routine screen must not state or imply the disposition. Detailed fields remain unknown until the assessment is obtained. Both actions are universal catalog options with patient-specific results. A positive or ambiguous screen or another relevant safety clue makes the detailed assessment a high-value conditional objective whose reward exceeds its cost. After a negative screen with no other clue, the assessment ordinarily earns no clinical points and loses only its purchase cost. Buying the full assessment directly fulfills the safety-screen subobjective but not unrelated general-history objectives. Missing both levels when important suicide-related facts exist remains a major omission. Treat this point behavior as reviewed Developer opinion informed by the source rather than a guideline-authored formula. Disposition is co-primary. Unsafe under-escalation receives the worst consequence and may reduce the case payout to zero. Clearly unnecessary ED transfer receives a major over-escalation penalty, and unnecessary urgent assessment a smaller but meaningful penalty. Initial patients should use clear disposition states; deliberately ambiguous cases may define multiple accepted options later. One disposition mistake receives one combined itemized consequence rather than stacked duplicate penalties. Safety-planning history asks only whether the patient reports feeling able to participate. Preserve that response separately from the clinician's risk formulation and disposition decision. It may contribute to reviewed disposition appropriateness but must never determine disposition by itself.
resurfacingTrigger: When suicide or self-harm findings, safety prerequisites, or disposition scoring change.

title: Resolve NICE NG225 permission before rule extraction
proposedRouting: Keep the record bibliographic-only unless NICE grants the required AI/reuse permission. If permission is obtained, create separate clinical tickets for assessment facts and disposition rather than one blended self-harm rule.
guidance: NG225 is a relevant all-ages self-harm guideline and has current public metadata, but NICE's terms require approval and a licensing arrangement for AI use and can require permission for international reuse. PsychSim must not download or extract the guideline through the AI-assisted source workflow yet. This ticket is an access gate, not a request to infer recommendations from the title or landing page.
resurfacingTrigger: When written NICE reuse and AI-processing permission is received or the source terms materially change.

title: Separate APA BPD treatment guidance from diagnosis criteria
proposedRouting: Treat this as a future treatment source only after written AI-use permission. Preserve the separate future diagnostic-standard and affective-instability-scale records, and require BPD to be explicit or explicitly uncertain in a patient template.
guidance: The verified publication is the second-edition APA treatment guideline, published online in 2024 although APA's guideline index labels it 2025. It is not a substitute for a diagnostic-criteria source. APA expressly bars inputting guideline content into generative AI without written permission, so no full text or recommendation has been ingested. After access is resolved, review psychotherapy, medication, crisis, and comorbidity implications as separate rules; self-harm or affective instability must never create BPD by themselves.
resurfacingTrigger: When APA grants written AI-use permission or a separate reviewed BPD diagnostic standard is added.

title: Gate APA delirium guidance behind permission and game scope
proposedRouting: After written permission and a delirium patient family exist, review only the immediate snapshot decisions needed to recognize a medical-evaluation or transfer path. Do not build a longitudinal prevention or reassessment simulator.
guidance: The 2025 APA delirium guideline is bibliographically verified, but APA expressly bars inputting its guideline content into generative AI without written permission. No full text or recommendation has been ingested. Delirium is also outside the current low-level outpatient patient pool. A later rule pass should distinguish modeled acute cognitive findings, what the player has assessed, and the immediate disposition or workup consequence without forcing delirium screening into every ordinary depression case.
resurfacingTrigger: When APA grants written AI-use permission or a focused delirium/acute-cognitive-change patient family is proposed.

title: Confirm the CANMAT corrigendum has no clinical-rule impact
proposedRouting: Preserve the first-class correction relationship and corrected author metadata. No clinical rule, recommendation, case, or point change is required.
guidance: The primary correction page states that Lena S. Quilty was corrected to Lena C. Quilty. The parent catalog record and protected local extraction already use the corrected name. No recommendation, table, evidence statement, or clinical wording changed, so the existing CANMAT clinical tickets may proceed unchanged.
resurfacingTrigger: When a further correction, retraction, or updated CANMAT MDD guideline appears.

resolution.note: Verified against the primary SAGE correction page, PubMed, and the parent record. This is an author-name-only correction with no clinical-rule impact. The first-class corrects relationship remains, and the source-use decision stays metadata-only because the notice has no reusable licence.

title: Define when catatonia becomes relevant to a snapshot case
proposedRouting: Review triggers first, then immediate workup/disposition consequences, then any focused intervention options. Keep the rule dormant unless a patient template contains clues that make catatonia a fair question.
guidance: The BAP consensus guideline is CC BY and has been extracted locally with exact page chunks. It can support a future catatonia-relevant patient and an acute safety gate, but it should not become a universal checklist. Decide which prior history, severe syndrome, psychomotor findings, medical context, or treatment history makes missing catatonia a big miss in a question-bank snapshot. Preserve the guideline's evidence limitations in the provenance and do not claim a general screening rule before review.
reviewerNotes: Psychiatrist/developer direction: expose the named Bush-Francis Catatonia Rating Scale examination as a universally searchable Physical/Mental Status action. Make it point-relevant only when authored clues make catatonia a fair focused question; do not penalize omission in routine uncomplicated outpatient depression. Catatonia-focused patients should be weighted chiefly to inpatient, hospital, and consultation-liaison pools and be very rare in the routine outpatient pool. Setting weights are game-selection data, not epidemiologic claims. The original BFCRS publication and public University of Rochester resources require a separate reuse determination before exact item wording is copied into PsychSim. The normal player-facing result should display only the BFCRS score, without item details, interpretation, diagnosis, or disposition guidance. Preserve any item-level derivation only in internal structured data and the Developer audit.
resurfacingTrigger: When a catatonia-relevant patient, ECT history, severe mood episode, or acute psychomotor finding is added.

title: Verify BFCRS source and item-reuse permission
proposedRouting: Register the 1996 original publication and current authoritative BFCRS assessment materials as separate evidence records, determine their exact reuse terms, and only then add exact item wording or scoring anchors to the universal examination catalog.
guidance: The BFCRS name, 23-item structure, and 14-item screening subset are publicly documented, and University of Rochester publishes current assessment resources. Public accessibility is not an explicit license to reproduce the instrument text in PsychSim. Keep the future action and structured-result schema reserved, but do not copy item definitions, examination instructions, or scoring anchors until rights and version provenance are recorded.
resurfacingTrigger: When implementing the BFCRS catalog action, ingesting a scale source, or receiving written reuse clarification.

title: Resolve ACE GAD reuse before building a GAD family
proposedRouting: Obtain or document permission before source extraction. Then decide whether this Singapore guidance is the primary GAD treatment source, a contextual source, or one jurisdictional overlay alongside another diagnostic standard.
guidance: The 2025 Singapore ACE GAD guideline has useful verified scope metadata, but the site terms restrict reuse without permission and do not clearly authorize this AI-assisted ingestion workflow. No PDF or recommendation text was ingested. PsychSim also has only a shared anxiety-history action, not a reviewed GAD diagnosis family. When access is resolved, build the diagnosis file, patient template, and treatment guidance separately so common subthreshold anxiety remains possible without silently creating GAD.
resurfacingTrigger: When reuse permission is documented or a GAD diagnosis/patient family is proposed.

title: Keep ASAM benzodiazepine tapering metadata-only
proposedRouting: Do not ingest ASAM text under the current terms. If written permission is obtained later, use it for focused benzodiazepine continuation, withdrawal, or taper best-next-step patients rather than as a general anxiety-treatment source.
guidance: ASAM's public page verifies the 2025 guideline's existence and tapering scope, but ASAM's terms prohibit inputting ASAM intellectual property into AI systems. PsychSim therefore stores metadata only and has not downloaded or parsed the PDF. The future gameplay fit is a narrow snapshot where existing benzodiazepine exposure, physical dependence, withdrawal risk, or an unsafe abrupt stop matters; it is not authority for starting benzodiazepines or for every anxiety presentation.
resurfacingTrigger: When ASAM grants written AI-use permission or a benzodiazepine/withdrawal patient family is proposed.

title: Source cyclothymia duration and near-miss constraints
proposedRouting: Find a legally reusable diagnostic source, then define a diagnosis-owned temporal criterion and two explicit patient-template relations: meets and below. Keep incidental symptom variation incapable of generating full mania.
guidance: The user wants duration to help distinguish a cyclothymic presentation from a deliberately subthreshold near miss, such as multi-year versus one-year symptom patterns. Do not infer exact criteria from unavailable DSM text or turn free background symptoms into a diagnosis. Review the exact age-specific temporal rule, source-use permission, and the shortest legible player-facing wording before enabling a cyclothymia case.
resurfacingTrigger: When a reusable classification or guideline source supplies cyclothymia temporal criteria.
